reasons: Directionally correct for us as the customer (IBM): the inserted covenant imposes insurance obligations on the vendor (MSL) and does not create risk for our side.

'Missing' status is supported — the only insurance references in the document are narrow property covers (replacement value for consigned Products, IBM-owned tooling insured by IBM, risk-of-loss relief on Loaned Items), none of which reach CGL, E&O, cyber or workers' compensation, so the clause set fails even the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M).
The rule's trigger is met on the facts cited: MSL occupies IBM premises, holds IBM and IBM-customer consigned inventory, and accesses IBM systems/customer data.

Redline tracks the model language closely (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, statutory workers' comp, certificates on request, survival for one year) and sensibly preserves the existing consigned-Products cover rather than displacing it — minimal, self-contained insertion.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, states the playbook position and offers the fallback limits; deterministic checks confirm the insurance obligation is present.

Minor, non-fatal: the insertion is anchored after an infringement/suspension remedy paragraph rather than clearly at the end of the General section — the new '16.22' heading should be confirmed against the actual General section numbering before sending.
